notes: limits.py holds plain SIGN_IN_LIMIT and DEMO_ADDRESS_LIMIT constants, read only by the _at_limit calls in check_sign_in and record_demo_creation, so M1 and M5 change the constants. views.sign_in locks the address's row, calls check_sign_in (which raises Limited), authenticates and records a failure in one limited_transaction, and starts the session afterwards: M2 authenticates first and checks the limit only for a failure, and M4 zeroes and saves the locked row on success inside the transaction (a zero count is an inactive window, so the next failure starts a new one). Migration 0003 only seeds the overall row, so no migration changes. M3 reads the first X-Forwarded-For entry, falling back to REMOTE_ADDR, in limits.client_address, called by address_key,, the one client-address function both per-address limits use.
